summary: Yasuro Abe specializes in Japanology, religious studies, and Buddhist studies. He studied at Wako University and Otani University, and held academic posts at Osaka, Otemae, Nagoya, and Ryukoku universities, as well as the International Research Center for Japanese Studies.

Yasusaburo Sakaki was an Indologist and linguist who studied at the University of Tokyo from around 1891 to 1895. He held posts at the University of Tokyo (~1898–1903) and Kyushu University (~1906–1929), and taught Gikyo Ito.

Yasushi Endo works in Indology and philosophy. He held positions at Nagoya University, Aichi Bunkyo University (attested 2000–2004), and Shitennoji University, where he was a professor (attested 2000).

Yasutaka Muroya is a scholar in Indology and philosophy. He has held research posts at the University of Vienna (attested 2007), the University of Leipzig (attested 2015), and the Institute for the Cultural and Intellectual History of Asia (attested 2016–2022).

Yasutoshi Murakami is a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Tohoku University. He held posts at Koyasan University and Yamaguchi University, and served as president of the Association of Esoteric Buddhist Studies (attested 2004).
Yawen Yang is a Buddhist studies scholar who completed an MA at Fo Guang University under the supervision of Yongdong Shi (attested 2009).
Yellava Subbarayalu is an Indologist, historian, and archaeologist. He served as a professor at Tamil University and as a researcher at the French Institute of Pondicherry (attested 2015).

Yeshe Thupten worked in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. In 1982, he held a post at Middlebury College and served as a visiting scholar at the University of Virginia, where he taught Donald S. Lopez Jr., Daniel Cozort, and Joe Bransford Wilson.

Yeshi Dhonden specialized in Tibetology. He studied at the Chakpori Institute of Tibetan Medicine under Khyenrab Norbu. In 1961, he founded Men-Tsee-Khang, serving as its director until 1966, and taught Elisabeth Finckh, Marsha Woolf, and Eliot Tokar.
Yi-hsun Huang specializes in Buddhist studies and sinology. She earned her PhD at the University of Virginia under Paul Groner and has taught Huidi Zeng.

Yifa works in Buddhist studies. She studied at National Taiwan University, University of Hawaiʻi at Mānoa, and Yale University under Stanley Weinstein, also studying under Hsing Yun. She held posts at University of the West, visited Harvard, and founded Woodenfish Foundation.
Yifan Zhang is a scholar in Buddhist studies, religious studies, and Tibetology. As of 2026, Zhang is a PhD student and faculty member at Ghent University.

Yigal Bronner is an Indologist who studied at Hebrew University of Jerusalem and the University of Chicago under Sheldon Pollock. He held an associate professorship at Hebrew University around 2010 and taught Whitney Cox and Roy Tzohar.

Yijie Tang specialized in philosophy, sinology, and Buddhist studies. After studying at Peking University (~1947–1951), he served there as professor (~1956–2014), held a post at Stanford University (~1989–1990), and founded the International Academy of Chinese Culture.

Yiliang Zhou worked in history, archaeology, Buddhist studies, and sinology. He studied at Fu Jen Catholic University, Yenching University under Yinke Chen, and Harvard University. He later served as a professor at Peking University (~1952–2001).

Ying-Kuang Chu was an expert in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He studied at Hangzhou Chicheng Public School and under Nordan Hutuktu, Bai Puren, Nona Hutuktu, and Gangkar Rinpoche. Chu also taught Shek-Wing Tam and Yui Chi Lau.

Ying-shih Yü was a sinologist, historian, and philosopher. Educated at Yenching, New Asia College, and Harvard, he held professorships at Harvard, Yale, and Princeton, and served as head of New Asia College and Pro-Vice-Chancellor of CUHK.

Yinggang Sun works in history, archaeology, Buddhist studies, and sinology. He has held posts at Fudan University (attested 2014) and served as a research fellow at the International Institute for Buddhist Studies (attested 2026).

Yingshan Chen works in Buddhist studies and philosophy. Chen held a professorship at the Chung-Hwa Institute of Buddhist Studies (attested 1996) and became an honorary research fellow there upon retiring in February 2023.

Yinke Chen was a sinologist, historian, and linguist who studied widely, including at Berlin and Harvard under Charles Rockwell Lanman. He held professorships at Tsinghua, Peking, National Southwestern Associated, Lingnan, and Sun Yat-sen universities, and taught Yiliang Zhou.
